title: QUIC Version Negotiation Runner Architecture
purpose: Describe the reserved-version versionnegotiation runner path, including the client initial-version override and root-URL dispatch, without expanding the major peer matrix or any HTTP/3 lane.
design_summary: The harness now recognizes versionnegotiation as a supported testcase on both client and server roles and routes it through a reserved-version probe path instead of the transfer-oriented handshake path. The client-side runtime accepts an internal supported-version override so its Initial packet can use a reserved version and elicit Version Negotiation, while the server-side listener treats the documented root URL as valid dispatch input and completes when the version-negotiation exchange is observed. The major-peer matrix is intentionally unchanged; this architecture is about the interop runner path only.
alternatives_considered: Treat versionnegotiation as a new public transport API. Rejected because the change belongs in the internal harness and client bootstrap seam, not the public API surface.
Expose versionnegotiation through the major peer matrix immediately. Rejected because that profile is intentionally scoped to handshake, retry, transfer, keyupdate, and resumption.
Leave the helper inventory claim unbacked by source. Rejected because the inventory must not outpace the harness dispatch surface.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The testcase must continue to reject unsupported or malformed runner input with the same exit-code semantics as the other supported harness cases.
The helper inventory should not be treated as support evidence without matching harness dispatch and a live runner proof bundle.
HTTP/3, 0-RTT, resumption, key update, and migration behavior remain governed by their own requirements.
data_and_state_considerations: Versionnegotiation uses the same local harness environment parsing and per-cell artifact capture as the existing supported cells, but its client bootstrap must pass a reserved supported-version override into the internal runtime seam and its server-side proof path must not depend on transfer-path derivation. No upstream runner repository changes are required.
risks: Log-text drift can create false negatives if the testcase name is not threaded through the dedicated version-negotiation path.
Readers may overread the supported/executed inventory cell as broader interop readiness.

supplemental_sections.heading: Scope
supplemental_sections.content: This design only closes the explicit versionnegotiation runner boundary. It does not expand the supported major-peer matrix or any HTTP/3 lane.
